_doc: Hand-placed points on the paperdoll body frames (assets/sprites/characters/hero.png, in pixels of a frame_size frame from the top-left, facing right) that tools/art/paperdoll_layers.py can't find by itself. weapon: [x, y, angle] = the fist holding the weapon and the way a sword in it points (degrees clockwise from pointing right; 90 is straight down); omit it and the weapon goes on his back (back views, sit) or is put away. weapon_behind: true when that fist is on the far side of his body, so the weapon draws behind him. shield: [x, y] = the off hand, where the shield goes (on his arm, or on his back while climbing); omit it to hide the shield. front: "shield" on frames where the shield point's hand is the one nearest us (Cory 2026-10-12: weapons are always held in the front hand), so the weapon kinds hold there ([x, y, angle] in holds) and the shield goes on the weapon point's hand instead. head_tilt: how far the head is turned (degrees clockwise), 0 when upright. holds: how each other weapon kind is held: 'like' copies another kind's angles, 'angle' is the angle on any frame not listed, 'frames' gives an angle (or [x, y, angle] to move the fist) per frame, 'behind' lists frames where that kind draws behind him. Angles are the way the weapon points whatever slant its sheet drew it at (sword, wand and staff art is measured and straightened). On idle, move, jump, fall, land, crouch, hit and hurt frames every weapon points forward or straight up/down, never back (except run1-2, where his weapon arm swings back as he runs, and claws, which point along his forearm) (tests/unit/hero_pose_test.gd checks it). hands: [[x, y], ...] = the middle of each hand his gloves go on, on frames where the hands aren't the weapon fist and the shield point (back views, sit, lying down). Preview with python3 tools/art/paperdoll_layers.py --preview.

sword._doc: Held like the staff (Cory 2026-10-12: the staff is the model for every weapon): in the middle of his front fist, the hand nearest us, on every frame, at the staff's angle to his forearm on each frame, gripped by the hilt so the blade comes out the far side of his fist. It draws over everything but his fist (over his open hand too on fall, where we see his palm), so its fist cut-out is kept to the fist. Every frame copies the staff's [x, y, angle]; change the staff's and the sword's together.

wand._doc: Held like the staff (Cory 2026-10-12: the staff is the model for every weapon): in the middle of his front fist, the hand nearest us, on every frame, at the staff's angle to his forearm on each frame. It draws over everything but his fist (over his open hand too on fall, where we see his palm), so its fist cut-out is kept to the fist. Every frame copies the staff's [x, y, angle]; change the staff's, the sword's and the wand's together.

claw._doc: A claw is worn like a big glove: it covers his fist and keeps the same angle to his hand and forearm on every frame, pointing the way his forearm does (Cory 2026-10-11, 2026-10-12). It is on whichever hand is nearest the viewer, always drawn in front (Cory 2026-10-12: idle and walk1/walk3 the weapon fist; walk2/walk4, hurt and jump the other hand, at its shield point). Every frame gives [x, y, angle] (the fist and the claw's angle), so changes to the sword's hold never move the claw. Each angle is that forearm's direction, from elbow to fist, set by eye on the body frame. On idle3 and hit his fist is raised in front of his chest, so the claw points forward, level with that forearm, and never covers his face.

knuckle._doc: Held as the sword was before swords were moved onto the staff's holds; unchanged until wands/knuckles get their own turn.

bow._doc: Held like the staff (Cory 2026-10-12: the staff is the model for every weapon): by the middle of its riser in the middle of his front fist, the hand nearest us, on every frame, at the staff's place on each frame, its belly away from him and its string toward him. It lies across his forearm, 5 degrees past square (the forearm's angle + 5, the staff's + 90), so it stands upright when his arm is held out to shoot and lies low and level when his arm hangs. Where his fist comes up in front of his chest (idle3, hit, hurt, run1, run3, run4) that would put it across his face, so there it lies level (80). Sit lies level on his knee and crouch keeps the forearm angle in front with his hand on top (Cory, bows thread). forearm: the way his forearm points on each frame (elbow to fist; the staff's angle + 85, or - 95 on fall), so his forearm draws over the bow's string (weapons.forearm_mask). It draws over everything but his fist and forearm (over his open hand too on fall, where we see his palm). Change the staff's and the bow's together.

staff._doc: Held like a MapleStory mage's staff (Cory's reference 2026-10-12): gripped low on the handle (STAFF_GRIP in paperdoll/common.py), in the hand nearest the viewer (the same fists as the claw: idle1 and walk1/walk3 the weapon fist; walk2/walk4, hurt and crouch the other hand; jump the weapon fist (Cory 14:43Z); on its knee when he sits, in his hand when he lies fainted), drawn in front of him with his fingers over the shaft. It keeps one angle to his forearm on every frame: each angle is that frame's forearm direction (the claw's, set by eye) -85 degrees, so on idle its head points forward and a little down; Every angle is exact, fall included. On fall, where his arm swings up behind him, the staff's head stays up out of the thumb side of his fist (the forearm's angle + 95) so it is never upside down; on jump it keeps the usual angle (Cory 14:49Z). On idle3 and the run frames the staff sits in the middle of his front fist at his forearm's exact angle, drawn over his body with his fingers over the shaft (Cory 15:29Z): run1, run3 and run4 in his forward fist, run2 in the hand swung back. On land his front arm hangs straight down, so the staff lies level in that fist; slash1 sits in the middle of the fist (Cory 15:38Z). On fall we see the inside of his raised hand, so the staff lies over his palm rather than under his fingers ('palm'; Cory 15:43Z); on hit it sits in the middle of his raised fist. Walking it is always in his front hand (Cory 15:55Z: never the wrong hand), and the walk frames ease toward one another so the hand change isn't jarring (Cory 15:47Z): walk1/walk3 a little above the forearm angle, walk2/walk4 turned less (Cory 15:55Z). It draws over everything but his fist (Cory 15:56Z: weapons in front of everything besides hands; over the hand too when we see his palm), so its fist cut-out ('fist', head radii) is kept to his fist and never cuts the staff where his shirt is.

gun._doc: A gun is held like a pistol: its grip in his fist with his fingers over it, its barrel along his forearm, at the same angle to his hand and forearm on every frame (Cory 2026-10-12: all one-handed weapons keep their angle to the forearm in every animation). It is in whichever hand is nearest the viewer, always drawn in front, at the same points as the claw (the weapon fist; walk2, walk4, hurt and jump the other hand, at its shield point), and each angle is that forearm's direction, from elbow to fist, set by eye (the claw's). When he fires (attack2, slash2, the frames the gun animation plays) his arm is out level, so the gun is level. On idle3 and hit his fist is raised in front of his chest, his forearm level across it: the gun sits in that fist (a little further out than the claw's point, which is on his wrist) pointing forward, in front like every other frame (behind him it would no longer be in his hand). Sitting it rests in his front hand on his knee, lying fainted in his hand at his side (in hand on every frame but climbing; none while he levels up, for every kind). Every frame gives [x, y, angle], so changes to the sword's hold never move the gun. A gun painted slanting is turned level first (barrel_tilt).
